decisions.quote:
The

present study sought to replicate and extend the work of Tragesser, Bruns, and

Disorbio (2010) who examined depression as a potential mediator of the link

between BPD and pain in a nonclinical sample. A three-path mediation model

of the sequence: BP features → depression → pain catastrophizing → pain sever-
ity provided the working hypothesis for the present study. Mediational analyses,

employing percentile bootstrapping, revealed a signicant three-path mediated

effect. The present study not only successfully replicated the ndings of Tragesser,

Bruns, & Disorbio (2010), but, by including pain catastrophizing, expands our

nascent understanding of how key individual differences mediate the BPD—pain

severity connection.
decisions.reason: The record is a replication collecting new survey data (final N = 500 students) to re-test and extend Tragesser, Bruns, & Disorbio (2010). Resolving the dependent original identity confirms it matches Tragesser et al. (2010). The authors state an explicit overall replication verdict in the abstract (and reiterate in the discussion, p. 396, lines 609-612, backed by the significant simple mediation path Borderline Features -> Depression -> Pain Severity, point estimate = 0.286, 95% CI [0.097, 0.525] in Table 2, and non-significant direct effect supporting full mediation, p = 0.172) that the study successfully replicated the findings of Tragesser, Bruns, & Disorbio (2010). Both shipped and blind codings accurately record 'successful'.
